title: Terrorism declined globally in 2025 but became more concentrated in conflict zones, borderlands, and youth radicalisation pathways
source_unit: Institute for Economics & Peace, Global Terrorism Index 2026
geography: 163 countries covering 99.7 percent of the world population, with global, regional, borderland, conflict, and youth-radicalisation comparisons

denominator.unit: countries ranked by the Global Terrorism Index

terrorism_deaths.unit: people killed in terrorist attacks in 2025

deaths_change.unit: percent change in terrorism deaths from the prior year

incidents_change.unit: percent change in terrorism incidents from the prior year

measurement.value: GTI scores combine incidents, fatalities, injuries, and hostages with a five-year weighting

observations.method: IEP Global Terrorism Index using TerrorismTracker event records and four indicators weighted over five years: incidents, fatalities, injuries, and hostages.
observations.uncertainty: Counts depend on event definitions, source coverage, attribution, and reporting; a global decline can coexist with regional escalation and does not imply broad subjective safety.
observations.subgroup: Civilians, communities in conflict-affected countries, governments, security institutions, and populations exposed to terrorism or counterterrorism.
observations.counterinterpretation: The 2025 decline is a meaningful improvement in aggregate impact even if the report warns that it may be temporary and unevenly distributed.

denominator.unit: countries most impacted by terrorism in the GTI 2026 summary

sub_saharan_africa_share.value: more than half of global terrorism deaths occurred in sub-Saharan Africa in 2025

sub_saharan_africa_top_ten.unit: countries among the ten most impacted by terrorism located in sub-Saharan Africa

regional_shift.value: the epicentre of terrorism has shifted from the Middle East and North Africa toward the Sahel region of sub-Saharan Africa

observations.method: IEP regional and country comparison using GTI scores, incidents, fatalities, and longitudinal terrorism trends.
observations.uncertainty: Regional concentration is sensitive to conflict intensity, reporting, and the index's five-year weighting; it does not mean terrorism is absent elsewhere.
observations.subgroup: Communities in the Sahel and other conflict-affected regions, border populations, displaced people, local authorities, and humanitarian actors.
observations.counterinterpretation: Deaths fell in ten sub-Saharan African countries in 2025 even while the region remained the global epicentre, showing that aggregate concentration and local improvement can coexist.

observations.period: 2021-2025; youth and online radicalisation in Western countries

denominator.unit: terrorism investigations and fatal-attack synthesis for Europe and North America

youth_investigation_share.unit: percent of terror-related investigations involving children and adolescents in 2025

youth_investigation_change.unit: fold increase in youth terrorism investigations since 2021

radicalisation_timeline.value: radicalisation timelines have compressed from longer historical periods to a matter of weeks in the report's 2026 assessment

lone_wolf_share.unit: percent of fatal terrorist attacks in the West attributed to lone-wolf actors over the last five years

platform_route.value: extremist networks use algorithm-driven platforms and encrypted messaging to build bonds and move toward operational planning

observations.method: IEP analysis of terrorism investigations, attack patterns, radicalisation timelines, and online recruitment pathways.
observations.uncertainty: Investigation counts and radicalisation classifications do not identify causal platform effects, individual trajectories, or the prevalence of radical beliefs in the wider youth population.
observations.subgroup: Children and adolescents, isolated youth, families, schools, online platforms, law enforcement, community organizations, and victims of terrorism.
observations.counterinterpretation: Most young people exposed to harmful content do not become terrorists; prevention, support, digital literacy, and trusted relationships may interrupt risk pathways.

observations.period: 2007-2025; borderlands, state control, and recruitment conditions

denominator.unit: global terrorism geography and recruitment synthesis frame

within_100km.unit: percent of terrorist attacks occurring within 100 kilometres of an international border in 2025

borderland_pattern.value: persistent hotspots include the Colombia-Venezuela frontier, Afghanistan-Pakistan borderlands, Central Sahel tri-border, and Lake Chad Basin

human_rights_abuse_motivation.unit: percent of sub-Saharan African recruits citing human-rights abuses by state security forces as the final catalyst for joining, in the report's synthesis

job_opportunity_motivation.unit: percent of voluntary recruits citing a total lack of job opportunities as their primary motivation in the report's synthesis

state_control.value: weak state control, porous borders, under-governed territory, and connected cross-border communities can create recruitment and operating spaces

observations.method: IEP spatial and thematic analysis of terrorism events, border proximity, governance conditions, and reported recruitment motivations.
observations.uncertainty: Recruitment-motivation shares depend on available study and reporting frames; they do not establish one universal cause or justify treating all border communities as risky.
observations.subgroup: Border communities, young people, people facing abuses or unemployment, local authorities, security forces, and cross-border populations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Borderlands can also support trade, family ties, mobility, and peacebuilding; weak state presence is not equivalent to community support for terrorism.

related_sources.claim: IEP GTI 2026 briefing provides global results, borderland, youth-radicalisation, and trend context.
IEP GTI 2026 press release provides headline death, incident, youth, borderland, and regional findings.

boundary: This record adds a terrorism route across global decline, regional concentration, conflict linkage, borderlands, youth radicalisation, online pathways, governance, and employment conditions. It uses aggregate IEP index measures and report synthesis, not respondent-level radicalisation histories, individual victim files, raw case-management records, causal platform effects, or proof that any correlate is a universal cause of terrorism.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official IEP GTI 2026 page, press release, briefing, and index methodology reviewed for scope, indicators, global 2025 totals, regional concentration, Pakistan, youth radicalisation, lone-wolf attacks, border proximity, and recruitment conditions.
